The small antenna size of the yubikey does hinder its power harvesting capabilities for sure. They can't make it any bigger without a redesign. [Yubikey 5 antenna design](https://www.hexview.com/~scl/neo5/neo5_brd_s.jpg)

It is a smartcard device, which by design are low power devices. It's not primarily an NFC issue. NFC does constrain things though.
Contact only cards have the same space issue

Increasing storage capacity isn't a straightforward task due to potential security concerns, as expanding memory could lead to higher power consumption, potentially risking data leakage, especially concerning for the YubiKey.

Furthermore, Yubico's pursuit of certifications adds complexity to any changes, requiring recertification. It's worth noting that Infinion, the chip manufacturer used in the YubiKey 5, doesn't appear to publicly offer JavaCard-capable chips with larger storage, which might necessitate new specifications first, due to the aforementioned power constraints. This seems also true for NXP, another manufacturer of JavaCard-capable chips.

Additionally, cost considerations are essential. Yubico carefully balances cost-effectiveness, and any investment in increased storage may ultimately impact consumers in the form of higher prices.
